chapter: Sandlot baseball and New Orleans sports
title: Armstrong's Secret Nine and escorting Louis Armstrong as Zulu king, 1949
summary: Asked about Armstrong's baseball team, Tex says he did not know the players but drove for Armstrong as Zulu king in 1949, and describes the Zulu club's growth.

venues.name: Zulu Social Aid and Pleasure Club

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah, he financed that team. Did you know any of the players in that? No, I didn't. I did not know any of the players. Because I've always looked at that photograph and I'm wondering who those players are, where of the Zulu club.
No, it could have been, maybe that was before my time. See, I've been around the Zulu since 1949, I wasn't an official member of the Zulu club.

I was an escort for Louis Armstrong in 1949 when he was a king because I drove one of the automobiles for him and I was an escort for his wife also. And I tell you, those were the good old days but not about the baseball players for the Zulu club. See, I was an honor, I remember I just started paying dues around about, I guess about 25, 30 years ago or something like that when I left town and came back and they needed money. And see what they did, the Zulus used to beg for money in the community from various businesses of friends and most of their white friends and a few blacks. But today, the Zulu organization is a worldwide international organization. They support themselves. We have doctors, lawyers, professional people like myself, engineers, technicians, and then we are integrated. We have about 10 or 12 of them. I want to tape some of that.
